findings.description: What is worth changing, one finding each. Empty when nothing is: a finding invented to look thorough costs a round.

file.description: The file, by path from the workspace root.

line.description: The line it is about; null when it is about something absent, such as a test nobody wrote.

kind.description: What kind of finding: `placement`, code in a boundary the repository's own rules give to another concern, or built elsewhere than the spec placed it; `behaviour`, a wrong result; `test`, a rule unproven, or a test that passes for nothing; `limit`, a ceiling raised or a size broken; `scope`, done what the spec did not ask, or left out what it asked; `other`, none of these.

rule.description: The repository rule the finding cites: the file that states or holds it, and its words. Null when it cites none; never null for a `placement` finding.

what.description: What goes wrong, concretely: the input or the case, and the wrong result.

mutants.description: Every `wf mutants:` line handed to you under What implement's check said, in its `reported`, each quoted whole, with your judgement of it. Empty only when `reported` holds none. When the section says `reported` is partial, still quote every `wf mutants:` line it holds, and say in a finding that lines printed earlier may be missing.

line.description: The `wf mutants:` line, quoted whole as the check printed it.

proves.description: true when the mutant breaks the rule it names, so the test that killed it proves that rule; false when it only breaks the file, or proves nothing the change adds.

why.description: Why, in a sentence: the rule the mutant breaks, or what it breaks instead.

again.description: true when a finding is worth another round: the engineer is handed your findings and the change comes back to you. false when it is done as far as a review can tell.
